text:
sam: Heads-up: after last night's CUDA driver push to h100 pool in us-west-2 we're seeing a spike in Triton/TensorRT plugin crashes + FlashAttention PTX rejects. Errors started ~03:10 UTC.

maya: saw alerts too. Canary jobs on canary-h100-1 failed 6/6 with runtime errors from xformers/flashattn kernels.

ethan: stack trace in pods shows `invalid PTX: checksum mismatch` when loading compiled kernels; TRT returns `TRT_INTERNAL_ERROR` during engine init. Pasting log from one failed pod:````
[2026-03-12T03:12:45Z] TRT: Engine create failed: invalid PTX checksum for module flash_attn_kernels.ptx
[2026-03-12T03:12:45Z] xformers: failed to load kernel flash_attn_fwd
[2026-03-12T03:12:45Z] torch: Caught runtime error: TRT_INTERNAL_ERROR
````

jules: Which driver version rolled? Ops PR showed nvidia-driver 535.52 -> 538.13 last night.

ana: @jules it's 538.13 on h100 instances in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. canaries in us-east-1 still on 535.x and are fine.

maya: So it's likely the new driver/ptx toolchain changed the generated PTX expectations. TRT/xformers compiled kernels that matched 535 are failing under 538.

sam: Impact: ~12% of h100 GPU pool in us-west-2 failing model launches; autoscaler keeps adding capacity but pods immediately crash -> wasted vCPU/GPU minutes. Cost impact estimate: ~$1.2k so far for the failed restarts.

ethan: Repro steps I ran: pull a Docker image with torch-xformers and run a micro-bench that triggers flashattn kernel compile; with driver 538 logs show `ptx checksum` rejects. On 535 image it loads fine.

maya: Any quick workaround? Maybe force software fallback to non-flash kernel or disable TRT engine caching?

jules: We can set env var XFORMERS_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 for affected deployments, and set TRT_FORCE_FALLBACK=1 for models using TensorRT to avoid engine-building path — but perf will drop.

ethan: Created a patch to k8s deployment template to inject XFORMERS_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 and TRT_ALLOW_COMPAT_FALLBACK=1 behind a feature flag. I'll open canary.

ci-bot: Build pipeline triggered: docker-image:gpu-serving:v2026-03-12-0742 -> pushed to staging registry.

maya: We should also opt to hotfix driver on a small subset to rollback to 535 in us-west-2 canary nodes while we validate the env var approach. Rolling rollback request incoming to infra.

ana: Rolling rollback may take 30-45m for node drain + reprovisioning. If we rollback entire pool we'll lose the new kernel fixes (but immediate availability trumps that).

sam: Agreed. Plan: 1) patch deployments to disable flashattn/TRT engine build (low-risk, quick) 2) rollback driver on a tiny worker pool (canary) to confirm that fixes load success 3) coordinate vendor ticket with NVIDIA + TRT team for PTX checksum regression 4) schedule a staged re-roll with more fine-grained kernel/ptx validation.

jules: Created internal incident in incidents channel: INC-2026-032. Linking here: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-032

ethan: Note: some models still crash even with XFORMERS_DISABLE_FLASHATTN because they rely on custom Triton plugins compiled against 535 libcublas kernels. We might need to rebuild plugins with new toolchain or pin plugin loading to legacy ABI.

maya: For short term, add a node selector for workloads that must use rebuilt plugins to run on 535 nodes only. We'll tag those nodes `gpu.toolchain=535-legacy`.

sam: Who's owning communication to customer success? Affected customers are a small set of enterprise tenants in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 using H100 Dedicated. We need messages about degraded performance and mitigation.

ana: I'll draft CS note and send to sales/AMs. Mention rollback and perf hit from disabling flash kernels.

jules: Ops rollback started on canary pool at 03:40 UTC. ETA ~40m. Monitoring RTT and TRT engine load counts.

ci-bot: Canary rollback job completed on 03:55 UTC: 3 nodes reprovisioned -> driver 535.x

ethan: Re-ran canary tests on nodes with 535 -> success: engines load, flashattn kernels present, no PTX checksum errors.

maya: Good signal. We'll keep the deployment env var in staging for broader cluster while vendor investigates.

sam: Follow-ups: - Eth: open GH issue on torch-xformers with minimal repro and attach PTX diff between 535/538 toolchains - Jules: coordinate with infra to craft safe staged rollback policy and capacity reservation to avoid autoscaler thrash - Nana: CS/Sales update - Maya: prepare perf dashboard noting fallback perf penalty (~+25% latency, -18% throughput)

ethan: Opening GH/INC tickets now. GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-repro/issues/289 INC updated.

jules: Also add a canary smoke that validates PTX load on driver change before we roll the rest of fleet. Add to canary playbook: deploy image -> run TRT engine build test -> verify no PTX rejects in logs -> proceed.

maya: Agreed. I'll add that to the release runbook.

sam: Thanks all. If vendor provides patched driver/kernel we'll coordinate small staged rollout with canary tests and plugin rebuilds. For now cluster is stabilized with mixed driver pools + env fallback.

ana: closing loop: cost of mitigation so far added to INC-2026-032. We'll update once NVIDIA responds. :spiral_note_pad:
